text:
anya: Heads-up — saw a weird KV residency spike on mistral-mqa when we hit long multi-turn sessions. memory climbs steadily then drops suddenly with lots of page faults. anyone else?
phil: saw similar on staging a few hours ago, looked like batch coalescing + rope scaling interaction. short repro attached.
ravi: can you paste logs? curious if kernel selector changed recently.
anya: paste logs below — this is from a dedicated node running kernel-selector v2.3.5 -> selected kernels flip between `mmt4_gemm` and `generic_gemm` during the surge.
```
[2024-11-12T09:42:15Z] model=mistral-mqa seq=4096 req_id=abc123 selected_kernel=mmt4_gemm opt=fp16 kv_residency_bytes=1.2G page_faults=8
[2024-11-12T09:42:18Z] model=mistral-mqa seq=4096 selected_kernel=generic_gemm opt=fp16 kv_residency_bytes=1.9G page_faults=112 fallback_reason=page_fault_rate>threshold
[2024-11-12T09:42:21Z] model=mistral-mqa seq=4096 selected_kernel=mmt4_gemm kv_residency_bytes=800M page_faults=4 recovery=cache_coalesce
```
maria: interesting — the jump to 1.9G coincides with a batch join where two long contexts merged. rope scaling doubled effective position embeddings, and MQA slots grew.
perf-bot: perf/regression detected on node infra-ded-07. metric=kv_page_fault_rate increased 14x over baseline (p<0.01). see run: https://perf.redwood/2145678901
phil: I think it's two things: (1) kernel-selector heuristics pick a kernel optimized for short batches when batch-topology changes mid-request; (2) KV allocator doesn't compact when MQA introduces additional slots -> fragmentation + page growth.
anya: repro steps I used:
* start dedicated node with qwen/llama disabled
* load Mistral-MQA model with seq=4096, enable rope scaling simulator (x2)
* send interleaved short and long prompts, batcher config: continuous batching ON, batch_timeout=8ms

Result: memory climbs, page faults spike, runtime falls back to generic kernels and latency doubles.
ravi: can you capture /proc/vmstat and slabinfo during the spike? particularly `nr_active_file` and `slab_page_allocs`. also KV cache journal shows many small allocations.
anya: pasted snippets: 
```
/proc/vmstat: pgfault  182394 pgmajfault 0 nr_free_pages 12345
/proc/slabinfo: kv_page_cache  12345  23456  128  4096  12  234  0  0 0
```
phil: that slab line looks like fragmentation: object size 128, high slab count. suggests many small allocations instead of coalesced region. can we try forcing `kv_alloc_batch=1` to see if it reduces churn?
maria: note: this issue only triggered on MQA variants; I ran the same on Llama-MQA and it didn't escalate as badly. hypothesis: Mistral's attention pattern + rope scaling creates lots of short-lived KV fragments that don't get reused.
ravi: I pushed a micro-patch to kernel-selector to add a 'kv_stability' signal: prefer kernels that avoid transient allocations when page_fault_rate > 50/s. rolling to staging now.
anya: nice, also toggled continuous batching off and the spike vanished in quick smoke. so batching heuristics amplify it.
phil: we should add a compact-on-evict path in KV manager that coalesces adjacent free pages when fragmentation crosses threshold. probably gated behind a feature flag.
maria: agree. add an integration test that simulates rope-scaling (x2/x4) + bursty joins to catch regression.
perf-bot: experiment 2145678901-kv-stability deployed to staging. results in 2hr run: kv_page_fault_rate reduced 78%, p99 latency improved 24%.
anya: great. next steps:
- ravi: keep kernel-selector patch on staging for 48h and capture long-run memory profile.
- phil: prototype KV compaction and run perf harness against MQA/Mistral/Qwen. include Llama baseline.
- maria: add test vectors for rope scaling + mixed batch topologies.
- i'll document hotfix rollback plan and alert thresholds.
phil: FYI: discovered an oddity — QWEN-GQA shows similar but with slower growth (likely due to different slot packing). will add to matrix.
ravi: if compaction hurts p50, consider async background compaction when load < 60%. avoid compaction during heavy tail.
anya: thanks team — filing follow-up ticket: https://redwood.atlassian/browse/INF-7921 with logs and perf links. we'll sync tomorrow @10am. :thumbsup:
